doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Sketching and watercolors during downtime
summary: Parker carries a portable watercolor set and sketchbook to sessions and gigs to stay focused, including sketching Shawn Pelton in Soho.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Let me talk about — I went to your website that was just for your visual art and I scrolled — it said sketch books. And I scrolled down and I said you have almost as many sketch books as you do LP credits. It’s a great idea. And it made me think — you probably are aware that both Milt Hinton and Joe Wilder carried a camera wherever they went. And they have just these kinds of pictures that no one else would get. And I was wondering, with all the — this question I have found the answer to — how did you find time to paint like this and you take it with you is that correct?

Absolutely. I have a little Winsor Newton portable watercolor set that fits in with my cymbals and stick bag and I have a sketch book always. And there’s often downtime, you know after the sound check or between takes sometimes or while the guitar players are overdubbing or — there is often a time where you want to stay focused, you don’t want to lose the momentum or the continuity of the session and I found that having a sketch book and drawing in between takes or in those downtime periods that often happen on a session for whatever reason — you know the machine broke down or waiting for a food delivery or whatever it is — that keeps me focused. And I like going out to hear live music. If I’m not on the gig myself I want to go hear other guys play, which I’ve done always, you know go hear somebody that I like and check them out live. So I mentioned Shawn Pelton, I just saw him a couple of weeks ago with a great bass player, Richard Hammond at some place in Soho that I’d never been and I had a good sight line and got out the sketch book and did some things with them. You know it’s hard to see everybody and people got in the way and stuff but it keeps me sort of concentrated on the music and the bar, the waiter knows don’t bother this guy he’s clearly involved in something else, just stick with my seltzer and lime please. Yeah, it works for me to have that alternative. You know keep the hand-eye coordination flowing until the next take.
